faq.a: Aamina is associated with the Arabic form أمينة, whose core sense is safe, secure, free from fear.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aamina?
faq.a: Aamina is associated with Arabic. Feminine of أمين; also the name of Āmina bint Wahb, the mother of the Prophet Muhammad, in the biographical (sīra) tradition.
Yes — the underlying form أمينة is Arabic.
Aamina can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Aamina should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. root أ م ن occurs in the Qur'an; أمينة is a normal Arabic feminine form

faq.q: What does Aamina mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Aamina is rendered آمنہ and carries the sense محفوظ، بے خوف، امن والی.

faq.q: What does Aamina mean in Persian?
faq.a: No verified Persian form was established for Aamina.
A romanized syllable approximation is aa-mi-na. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Aamina?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Aamina, aamina, amina. Script forms are آمنه, آمنہ, أمينة, आमिना.

faq.q: Is Aamina a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
